title: fix(cuda-graph): address shape-guard warmup regression causing OOM under continuous batching
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes: Fixes OOM regression in CUDA graph warmup when shape guards are enabled and continuous batching is active; reduces memory pressure during warmup and improves stability under concurrent workloads.
description: Context: a regression was observed after PRs that introduced shape-guarded CUDA graph capture/replay and warmup optimizations; under continuous batching with heterogeneous sequence lengths some warmup traces retained oversized tensors leading to peak OOMs on high-concurrency hosts. This PR diagnoses and fixes the regression. Root cause: the CUDA graph warmup path previously cached intermediate buffer allocations keyed only by capture-id and shape-guard tag; when continuous batching combined multiple capture shapes in-flight we could reuse a buffer sized for the max shape and retain it across captures, causing superlinear memory growth during warmup and when multiple streams concur. Changes: 1) make cuda_graph::WarmupBuffers keyed by exact capture shape + device/stream id to prevent accidental reuse across incompatible captures; 2) add explicit trim-path after warmup to release oversized temporary KV-cache buffers when a smaller capture shape is next used; 3) add a conservative upper-bound guard and fallback path that falls back to the kernel path if GPU memory pressure is detected during capture replay; 4) improve scheduler interaction so warmup tasks for capture/replay are serialized per-context to avoid concurrent warmups fighting for temporary buffers; 5) add regression tests and a perf canary to detect the previous OOM pattern. Testing: unit tests added for WarmupBuffers semantics; integration/perf canary run across toy and large models (gpt-like configs) shows ~20% reduction in peak GPU memory during warmup and stable throughput under continuous batching at 8 concurrent streams. CI: build, unit tests, lint and integration passed; perf-canary initially flagged a slight increase in latency for tiny sequences but we tuned the trim-path to reclaim memory without impacting median latency. Related work: references previous PRs that introduced the shape-guard warmup logic (pr-24567, pr-25095, pr-23890) and the rerun from ENG-6721. Notes: this is a low-risk runtime fix that adds a small serialization point for warmup tasks but dramatically improves stability; follow-up work is tracked under ENG-6810 to refine warmup concurrency heuristics.
